newsitem.title: USA: North America bunkers firm on supplies, crude hype.
newsitem.headline: North America bunkers firm on supplies, crude hype.

text.p: North American bunker prices stayed firm in cautious action supported by low stocks and fears of further crude oil spikes, traders said Tuesday.
Prices hotted up after the U.S. fired retaliatory missiles on Iraq last week, sending bunker prices some $12 higher in Los Angeles, and prices have largely not corrected since then.
"Sellers raised their numbers around the world, and buyers who waited are now having to cover," a West Coast trader said, adding that low stocks aggravated the situation.
Sellers who quoted reasonably low prices in the aftermath of the Iraq crisis also have to consider replacement costs.
Traders also noted a lack of arbitrage between various centers, with quotes mostly at similarly high levels.
Los Angeles 380 CST was at $110/111 a tonne, and 180 CST was pegged at $112/117 a tonne.
In New York Harbor, 380 CST crept up to $112/114, up about $4 from last week. The Norfolk hub was also strong with 380 CST at $115/116, and 180 CST at $120/121.
On the Gulf Coast, supplies were even tighter due to low inventories and a reluctance to restock until prices cooled.
Houston 380 CST was at $112/114 a tonne, and 180 CST was at $116/117 a tonne.
-- Jacqueline Wong, New York Energy Desk + 1 212 859-1620
